title: Machine-learning metabolomics identifies widespread promiscuous activities in Escherichia coli enzymes
summary: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested. Follow-up reconstruction assigned 22 reaction stoichiometries to 11 enzymes, with four reactions experimentally validated; examples include expanded nucleotide-substrate use by DeoA, cofactor and sugar promiscuity in NanK, and FMN dephosphorylation by CobC. Follow-up assays also found that pyrimidine-specific ribonucleoside hydrolase RihB acted on thymidine, guanosine and deoxyuridine, further extending its measured substrate range.
ai_technology: Machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier applied to enzyme metabolomics ion-trace data
organization: ETH Zurich; Weizmann Institute of Science; University Children’s Hospital Zurich and University of Zurich

evidence.tested: In vitro metabolomics of 667 purified E. coli enzymes, analyzed with a machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, indicated previously unrecognized promiscuous activities in 11% of enzymes tested.
evidence.unknown: The classifier operated at a 33% false-discovery rate; the 135 ion traces were putatively annotated, and only four of 22 reconstructed reaction stoichiometries were experimentally validated. Therefore the full 11% result is a set of candidate activities, not 11% independently confirmed enzyme functions. The RihB activities were prompted by a low-confidence potassium-thymidine-adduct trace and then tested directly with purified enzyme; they should be distinguished from the classifier’s higher-confidence hit set.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning-derived multivariate classifier, with a reported false-discovery rate of 33%, detected unexpected changes in metabolite ion traces in the enzyme assays and helped nominate candidate promiscuous activities. The researchers then reconstructed candidate reaction stoichiometries and experimentally validated four reactions.
